title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.34250v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. To evaluate and address EBU, we introduce MedSkill-E$^{2}$, a framework for evaluating and evolving skills for medical agents. We construct EBU-Bench, a challenging benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups and associated skills, to evaluate agents' ability to use available skills autonomously. We quantify the EBU gap as the difference in skill-use accuracy between autonomous use and explicitly guided reading and application of the same skill. On EBU-Bench,

translated_title: MedSkill-E²：医疗智能体技能的评估与演化
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地使用技能来获取领域知识并完成现实世界的任务。我们观察到，即使某项技能已经明确了任务所需的规则和流程，智能体在自主执行过程中仍可能无法有效应用它们，我们将这一现象称为“技能已启用但未被充分利用”（Enable But Underuse, EBU）。这一问题在医疗任务中尤为严重，因为忽视任何一个关键约束都可能导致看似合理但实际错误的结果。为了评估和解决EBU问题，我们提出了MedSkill-E²，一个用于评估和演化医疗智能体技能的框架。我们构建了EBU-Bench，一个具有挑战性的基准测试，涵盖12个医疗相关任务组及其关联技能，用于评估智能体自主使用可用技能的能力。我们将EBU差距量化为自主使用技能与在明确引导下阅读并应用同一技能之间技能使用准确率的差异。
tldr: 该论文提出了MedSkill-E²框架和EBU-Bench基准，首次发现并量化了医疗智能体中“技能已启用但未被充分利用”（EBU）现象，即智能体虽然拥有完成任务所需的技能，却在自主执行时无法有效应用，从而可能产生看似合理但实际错误的结果。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MedSkill-E² and the EBU-Bench benchmark to identify and quantify the "Enable But Underuse" (EBU) phenomenon, where medical agents fail to effectively apply available skills during autonomous execution, potentially producing plausible but incorrect results.
